The zeromotor

Sheet
27 of 56
Group
The second kind
Motion

The claim

Liquid ammonia boils far below the freezing point of water, so sea water is hot enough to raise ammonia vapour at more than four atmospheres. The vapour drives a piston. Gamgee held that it would cool as it expanded, turn back to liquid by itself, and be pumped round again. The United States Navy took an interest, since a ship driven this way would need no coal.

Why it stops

Vapour turns back to liquid only if it can hand its heat to something colder, and nothing on board is colder than the ammonia. The exhaust stays vapour, its pressure climbs until it matches the boiler, and the piston ends with the same push on both faces.
